extracted_concepts.name: Power Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: If f(x)=x^n where n is a real number, then f'(x)=nx^(n-1).

extracted_concepts.name: Constant Multiple Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: If c is a constant and f(x) is differentiable, then d/dx[cf(x)]=cf'(x).

extracted_concepts.name: Sum and Difference Rules
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: If f and g are differentiable, then d/dx[f(x)±g(x)]=f'(x)±g'(x).

extracted_concepts.name: Derivative of e^x
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx(e^x)=e^x; the exponential function is its own derivative.

extracted_concepts.name: Derivative of a^x
aliases: derivative of a to the x
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx(a^x)=a^x·ln a.

extracted_concepts.name: Number e
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The unique number for which lim_{h→0}(e^h-1)/h=1, making e^x the only function equal to its own derivative.

extracted_concepts.name: Differentiation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The process of finding the derivative of a function, representing the rate of change.

extracted_concepts.name: Antidifferentiation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The inverse operation of differentiation; finding a function whose derivative is a given function.

extracted_concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Connects differentiation and antidifferentiation as inverse operations.

extracted_concepts.name: Velocity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The derivative of position with respect to time: v(t)=s'(t).

extracted_concepts.name: Acceleration
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The derivative of velocity with respect to time: a(t)=v'(t)=s''(t).

extracted_concepts.name: Position function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function s(t) describing the position of an object as a function of time.

extracted_concepts.name: Marginal cost
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The derivative of the cost function: MC=C'(x).

extracted_concepts.name: Rate of change
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change of a function.

extracted_concepts.name: Tangent line approximation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Uses the derivative to estimate function values near a known point.

extracted_concepts.name: Exponential function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function of the form a^x, particularly e^x which equals its own derivative.

extracted_concepts.name: Polynomial
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function composed of terms with real exponents, differentiated using the Power Rule.

extracted_concepts.name: Differentiable function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function that has a derivative at every point in its domain.

extracted_concepts.name: Real number exponent
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: An exponent n that can be any real number, not just positive integers, in the Power Rule.

extracted_concepts.name: Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The limit of the difference quotient; represents the instantaneous rate of change of a function.

extracted_relations.evidence: The Power Rule applies to f(x)=x^n where n is a real number, requiring the function to be differentiable.

The tangent line approximation uses the derivative to estimate function values near a known point.
The derivative as a rate of change connects differentiation to real-world problems.
The Power Rule is a fundamental differentiation rule for polynomials and exponential functions.
The Constant Multiple Rule is one of the basic differentiation rules.
The Sum and Difference Rules are basic differentiation rules.
Derivatives of exponential functions are a key part of differentiation rules.
Derivatives of a^x are part of the differentiation rules for exponential functions.
The Power Rule extends to any real exponent, not just positive integers.
Derivatives of polynomials are computed using the Power Rule.
A derivative exists only for differentiable functions.
Velocity as derivative of position is an application of differentiation in physics.
Acceleration as derivative of velocity is an application of differentiation in physics.
Marginal cost is an application of differentiation in economics.
